english.title: Fail to notify the Secretary of State of possession of deactivated firearm
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), failed to give notice of possession of the deactivated firearm to the Secretary of State

(A)_[on or before the day of possession or as soon as reasonably practicable after possession]_
(B)_[describing the deactivated firearm by giving, if known, the make, calibre and serial number]_
(C)_[as to the name and address of the person giving notice]_
(D)_[as required by published postal or electronic means]_

where the transferor of the firearm had not given notice under regulation 2 of the Firearms Regulations 2019
english.legislation: Contrary to regulations3(1) and (6) of the Firearms Regulations 2019.

english.notes:
PLEASE NOTE: This offence is revoked as of 4th March 2026. However, following the savings provisions within regulation 5 of the Firearms (Revocation, Consequential Amendment and Saving Provision) Regulations 2026 an offence may still be committed after this date.

(i) The Secretary of State will be deemed to have been notified when notice has been given in line with regulation 3(3).
(ii) The offence will not apply where an individual has been in possession of the deactivated firearm for a period of 14 days or less.
(iii) The offence will not apply until 14/03/2021 in respect of deactivated firearms which came in to a person's possession before 14th September 2018.
(iv) There is a defence available for the offence under regulation 3(5) in circumstances where the individual accused can demonstrate they reasonably believed the transferor of the deactivated firearm had given, or would give notice of the transfer in accordance with regulation 2.
